guideTitle: The Best Standing Desks and Converters With Keyboard Trays
breadcrumbLabel: Best Standing Desks With Keyboard Trays
metaTitle: Best Standing Desks With Keyboard Trays: Desks, Converters and Add-Ons (2026)
metaDescription: We compared standing desks, converters and a clamp-on add-on by whether a keyboard tray is confirmed, tray size, desk depth and storage, and note which listings leave the tray unclear.
introParagraphs: A keyboard tray lowers the keyboard below the desktop, which helps when the desk surface sits too high for comfortable typing. Many ergonomics guides also favor a tray that tilts slightly away from you (negative tilt), though none of the listings here state their tilt angle, so check product photos or the seller's Q&A if that matters to you.

The products here fall into three types: full electric standing desks with a tray, tabletop converters that sit on an existing desk, and a clamp-on tray for a desk you already own. Two converters are included for their monitor features but do not clearly confirm a tray in their listings, and are marked as such.

Our comparison is based on published specifications, including desk size, tray description and storage, plus price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $42 to $220 at the time of writing.

offigo-55-u-shaped-keyboard-tray.badge: Best Desk With a Wraparound Surface
offigo-55-u-shaped-keyboard-tray.summary: A 55-inch U-shaped electric standing desk with a keyboard tray confirmed in its listing.
offigo-55-u-shaped-keyboard-tray.description:
The OffiGo is the full-desk pick for buyers who want a wraparound surface: a 55-inch U-shaped electric standing desk with a keyboard tray confirmed in the listing.

The U shape keeps monitors, documents and accessories within reach around you, and the tray sits below the main desktop for a lower typing position. It is well rated for its category.

The listing does not specify the tray's tilt or weight rating, and the U shape needs more floor space than a rectangular desk.
cons: Tilt and tray rating not listed
offigo-55-u-shaped-keyboard-tray.bestFor: Home offices that want a wraparound desk with a tray.
offigo-55-u-shaped-keyboard-tray.skipIf: You are short on floor space; the ErGear is a compact 44 x 24 inches.

vivo-36-v-series-converter-no-confirmed-.summary: A 36-inch dual-monitor converter whose listing does not confirm a keyboard tray.
vivo-36-v-series-converter-no-confirmed-.description:
The VIVO V Series is a 36-inch tabletop converter designed around dual monitors and a laptop, and its listing does not confirm a keyboard tray. It is included as a reference point because it is widely reviewed, not as a tray recommendation.

It uses a quick sit-to-stand mechanism and sits on an existing desk.

If you need a tray, the VIVO K Series costs less and confirms a wide tray in its listing.
cons: Costs more than the K Series
vivo-36-v-series-converter-no-confirmed-.bestFor: Buyers focused on a dual-monitor converter who will confirm tray details with the seller.
vivo-36-v-series-converter-no-confirmed-.skipIf: You need a confirmed tray; the VIVO K Series lists one.

vivo-32-k-series-wide-keyboard-tray.badge: Best Converter With a Confirmed Tray
vivo-32-k-series-wide-keyboard-tray.summary: A 32-inch converter with a wide keyboard tray confirmed in its listing, and a large review base.
vivo-32-k-series-wide-keyboard-tray.description:
The VIVO K Series is the converter we would start with: a 32-inch tabletop unit with a wide keyboard tray confirmed in its listing, for about $140 at the time of writing.

The upper deck takes dual monitors or a laptop, the tray sits below for typing, and it is the most widely reviewed product here.

The tilt angle is not stated, the tray layout is designed around a right-hand mouse, and a converter's tray reduces the depth available on top.
vivo-32-k-series-wide-keyboard-tray.bestFor: Buyers adding a sit-stand converter with a tray to an existing desk.
vivo-32-k-series-wide-keyboard-tray.skipIf: You want a larger tray; the SANODESK lists a large one.

vivo-42-converter-tray-unconfirmed.summary: A 42-inch converter with a dual monitor stand; the listing does not clearly confirm a tray.
vivo-42-converter-tray-unconfirmed.description:
This 42-inch VIVO converter's model number includes "KB", but its title and description describe a dual monitor stand and desk riser without stating a keyboard tray. We treat the tray as unconfirmed until verified with the seller or current photos.

Its documented strength is the dual monitor stand, listed for screens from 13 to 30 inches, on a converter that sits on an existing desk.

It is the most expensive converter here at the time of writing. If you need a confirmed tray, the VIVO K Series or SANODESK are clearer choices.
vivo-42-converter-tray-unconfirmed.bestFor: Buyers who mainly want a converter with a built-in dual monitor stand.
vivo-42-converter-tray-unconfirmed.skipIf: A confirmed tray matters; choose the VIVO K Series or SANODESK.

ergear-keyboard-tray-standing-desk.badge: Best Budget Standing Desk With Tray
ergear-keyboard-tray-standing-desk.summary: A 44 x 24-inch electric standing desk with a keyboard tray for about $150.
ergear-keyboard-tray-standing-desk.description:
The ErGear is the lower-cost full desk: a 44 x 24-inch electric standing desk with a keyboard tray confirmed in its listing.

Because the tray is part of a dedicated desk, the whole setup rises and falls together, rather than a converter stacked on another desk.

A 24-inch depth is moderate, and a tray reduces the legroom and usable depth further, so check the space you need for monitors. Tilt is not stated.
pros: Full desk with a tray at a low price
ergear-keyboard-tray-standing-desk.bestFor: Smaller rooms that want a dedicated standing desk with a tray.
ergear-keyboard-tray-standing-desk.skipIf: You want drawers; the AODK includes them.

aodk-55-drawers-keyboard-tray.summary: A 55-inch standing desk with drawers and a keyboard tray, in rustic brown.
aodk-55-drawers-keyboard-tray.description:
The AODK is the pick if you want storage built in: a 55-inch standing desk with drawers and a keyboard tray, both confirmed in the listing.

The wider top suits a dedicated home office, and the rustic brown finish may suit a room where a plain white or black desk would look out of place.

Check that the drawers and the tray do not get in each other's way, or in the way of your knees, at your sitting position. Tilt is not stated.
cons: Drawer and tray placement need checking
aodk-55-drawers-keyboard-tray.bestFor: Home offices that want a tray and storage in one desk.
aodk-55-drawers-keyboard-tray.skipIf: You want a smaller desk; the ErGear is 44 inches wide.

sanodesk-42-large-keyboard-tray.badge: Best Converter With a Large Tray
sanodesk-42-large-keyboard-tray.summary: A 42-inch electric converter with a large keyboard tray confirmed in its listing.
sanodesk-42-large-keyboard-tray.description:
The SANODESK is the converter to choose for more tray room: its listing confirms a large keyboard tray, which should leave space for a keyboard and a mouse.

It is a 42-inch electric converter with room for dual monitors or a laptop on the upper deck.

It has fewer buyer reviews than the VIVO converters, and the tilt angle is not stated.
sanodesk-42-large-keyboard-tray.bestFor: Converter buyers who want room for a keyboard and mouse on the tray.
sanodesk-42-large-keyboard-tray.skipIf: A long review record matters; the VIVO K Series is more widely reviewed.

ax-waber-standalone-keyboard-tray.summary: A clamp-on pull-out tray for adding a keyboard tray to a desk you already own.
ax-waber-standalone-keyboard-tray.description:
The AX WABER is not a desk or converter but a clamp-on keyboard tray, and it is the low-cost choice if your standing desk already works and only lacks a tray.

It has a 27.3-inch slide-out platform, about 32.5 inches wide including the clamps, and an adjustable C-clamp mount described as extra sturdy.

It needs a desk edge the clamps can grip, and the listing does not give a weight rating, so avoid leaning heavily on the front edge until you know how it holds up.
ax-waber-standalone-keyboard-tray.bestFor: Owners of a standing desk without a tray.
ax-waber-standalone-keyboard-tray.skipIf: Your desk has a thick apron or no clampable edge; check the clamp range first.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Six products here confirm a tray in their listings. The VIVO 36-inch V Series and 42-inch converter do not, and a model code alone should not be taken as confirmation.
A slight negative tilt is often recommended for wrist position. None of the listings state tilt, so check photos or ask the seller if it matters to you.
A tray takes space under the desk and can reduce legroom. On shallower desks, such as the 24-inch ErGear, measure what remains.
Wide or large trays (VIVO K Series, SANODESK) leave more room for a mouse beside the keyboard.
A full desk raises everything together; a converter sits on an existing desk; a clamp-on tray adds a tray to a desk you already own.

faq.q: Which products here confirm a keyboard tray?
faq.a: The OffiGo, VIVO K Series, ErGear, AODK, SANODESK and AX WABER. The VIVO 36-inch V Series and 42-inch converter do not clearly confirm one in their listings.
It means the tray's front edge is higher than the back, so the keyboard slopes slightly away from you. Many ergonomics guides favor it for wrist position. None of the listings here state their tilt.

faq.q: How much depth or legroom does a tray take?
faq.a: It depends on the tray and mount. Measure the tray's depth and position and compare them with your desk and knee clearance before ordering.

faq.q: Can I add a tray to a standing desk I already own?
faq.a: Yes. The AX WABER clamps to an existing desk. Check that your desk's edge suits a C-clamp.

faq.q: Will a tray flex if I rest my wrists on it?
faq.a: It may. Trays are usually rated for the weight of a keyboard and mouse, and resting your hands adds load at the front edge. None of the listings here give a tray weight rating.
None of the listings here confirm one. Left-handed buyers should check product photos closely.

bottomLine: If your desk already works, the AX WABER is the inexpensive way to add a tray. For a converter, the VIVO K Series is the confirmed-tray choice with the longest review record, and the SANODESK offers a larger tray.

For a full desk, the ErGear is the compact budget option, the AODK adds drawers, and the OffiGo gives a wraparound surface. The two VIVO converters without a confirmed tray are better treated as dual-monitor converters than as keyboard-tray desks.
